experts: Guided programmes, honest answers and a weekly pulse to keep your relationship growing.

A 2021 meta-analysis (93 studies, ~38,500 people, Mallory, Journal of Family Psychology) found sexual communication relates to sexual satisfaction (r≈.43) and relationship satisfaction (r≈.37). The quality of conversations mattered more than how often you talk or how much you disclose.
Used in: Talk First step in every session, the Talk About Sex programme, the Match tool, Weekly Check-in.

Muise, Giang & Impett (2014, Archives of Sexual Behavior): in two studies (about 335 people, and 101 couples tracked for three months) more time spent on affection after sex was linked to higher sexual satisfaction, and to relationship satisfaction on daily and longer-term measures.
Used in: the 10-minute Afterglow that ends every guided session.
Used in: the One New Thing step, Try Something New on the home page.

Sensate focus (Masters & Johnson) is a staple of sex therapy that removes performance pressure by separating touch from the goal of arousal. Evidence is mostly clinical and the technique is described inconsistently across the literature, so it is a well-regarded tool rather than a proven cure-all.
Used in: the Slow Touch step and the Slow Touch programme.

Widely used models (Basson's responsive desire; Bancroft & Janssen's dual control model popularised by Nagoski) describe desire as often arising after touch begins and as shaped by "accelerators" (what turns you on) and "brakes" (stress, worry). Many people feel desire only once they start.
Used in: Desire & Rhythm programme, planning date nights, low-pressure starts.

Used in: a forgiving "rhythm" (one rest day never breaks it) instead of a streak you can lose.
Why we avoid streak pressure

Research on gamification (for example Silverman et al., 2023, Journal of Consumer Research) found people who break a streak are more likely to quit, and tracking can turn enjoyable things into chores (Etkin, 2016). Guilt-based messages can backfire.
Used in: no guilt notifications, no lost-streak screens, an optional daily "time to be together" reminder, and a partner nudge instead of points as the main reason to return.

The strongest design for coming back is something meaningful from your partner: a message, an invitation, a shared plan. That is why Nudges, Secret Envelopes and shared date nights are the core of the return loop.
